speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) will continue to deliver good health outcomes for Singaporeans, while keeping costs affordable for individuals and sustainable for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have been able to achieve these objectives through the delivery of high-quality care, supported by a dedicated healthcare workforce and resilient infrastructure built up over the years, and a S+3M (subsidies, MediSave, MediShield Life, and MediFund) system that instils financial discipline while providing a safety net for patients who need it.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The COVID-19 crisis has given us new perspectives on our pandemic preparedness plans and public health capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Medical advancements are not only opening up new possibilities but also major challenges and dilemmas.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Singapore’s healthcare system is therefore at a pivotal phase of its transformation journey.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOH will set up a permanent Crisis Strategy and Operations Group, to maintain surge readiness for mid-sized outbreaks and other health emergencies, and to prepare healthcare institutions to be crisis-ready.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also maintain a healthcare reserve force, to expand surge capacity if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOH will continue to make progress on PREPARE, the Programme for Research in Epidemic Preparedness and Response, to develop our capabilities in global surveillance so we may better understand new and dangerous pathogens.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will implement our vaccine strategy, to secure an early supply of efficacious vaccines when another pandemic breaks out.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also review the Infectious Diseases Act (IDA) to deal with a wider range of public health situations, and better manage crisis communications.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to invest in healthcare infrastructure and expand our care capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This includes the Woodlands Health Campus, the Tan Tock Seng Hospital Integrated Care Hub, the Eastern Integrated Health Campus, and the redevelopment of Alexandra Hospital.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By 2030, we will build 10 more polyclinics, making a total of 32 polyclinics.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also expand the capacity of our nursing homes from 16,000 beds in 2020 to more than 31,000 beds in 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will invest heavily in IT, focusing on mission-critical national systems for hospital billing, drug ordering and dispensation, and the maintenance of national medical databases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With good training opportunities and career prospects, Singapore will remain competitive in attracting foreign healthcare manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: More opportunities will be made available for doctors to become Family Physicians and develop their competencies, such as through postgraduate family medicine training.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to upgrade the skills and knowledge of nurses and Allied Health Professionals, so that they can assume greater responsibilities, including in leading more clinical community care initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: While ageing and changes to our demography are inexorable, we can improve the health of our population through effective preventive care that spans the entire life of an individual.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will be a major focus in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will enhance mental health screening and psycho-emotional support for pregnant women and their spouses, and support families in cultivating healthy lifestyle habits from young.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As the child gets older, schools and preschools are important platforms to foster and sustain healthy habits.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will partner MOE and MSF closely, to incorporate health education in the school experience, and lay a strong foundation of health for our younger generation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For adults, Healthier SG will be the key strategy to encourage healthy living and deliver preventive care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Family doctors play an integral role in inculcating and strengthening good health habits, such a good diet, regular exercise, and routine health screenings and vaccinations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To support this effort, we are marshalling community resources and partners to organise physical activities in the community, and to reach out to residents and encourage them to enrol.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Through the Health Promotion Board, we will continue to drive efforts to reduce sugar and sodium intake, equip consumers with information to make healthier eating choices, manage the consumption of tobacco and nicotine, and promote smoking cessation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By emphasising preventive care, Healthier SG brings healthcare out of hospitals and clinics, and into the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are therefore updating the Healthcare Services Act, to make regulations services-centric, instead of focusing on the premise where care is delivered.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Similarly, we need to review our healthcare financing policies to make them more premise-neutral, and ensure support is available regardless of where care is sought.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For our seniors we need to make ageing in community the default, because it is the best way for them to stay socially engaged and active, and hence healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As part of the Forward Singapore exercise, we are studying the specific measures to enable this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also enhance financial support for palliative care and ensure sufficient capacity across all settings to meet growing needs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are in a period of major breakthroughs in medical science, especially in areas like precision medicine, gene editing, and artificial intelligence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For instance, with precision medicine, we can consider individual variations in genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors when predicting the health risks of individuals, and determine the most effective prevention and treatment strategies for them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At the same time, there will likely be a proliferation of experimental treatments, such as genetic therapies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to support and embrace technological advances but remain aware of the risks and pitfalls.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Experimental treatments tend to work only on a small minority, so mass deployment of new treatments must be subject to evidence-based clinical development and evaluation of cost and medical effectiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We may also need new legislation to safeguard moral and ethical standards in the practice of new medical technology such as precision medicine.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOH will undertake this long-term effort in partnership with researchers, physicians, economists, bioethicists, regulatory bodies, and the public, to reap the benefits of these new solutions.
